title: October operations at a fictional manufacturer
description: An eight-sheet synthetic model linking sales, production, purchasing, costs and cash for four products, three materials and sixteen orders.

regions.title: Cash and operating assumptions
regions.description: Enter collection and payment rates and opening cash here.

regions.title: Opening material stock
regions.description: Purchasing deducts this stock from the material requirement.

regions.title: Product specifications
regions.description: List prices, material usage, labor costs and finished-goods inventory targets.

regions.title: Material specifications
regions.description: Costing and Purchasing use the same material prices.

regions.title: Sixteen customer orders
regions.description: Deduct returned units and apply each order’s discount to the list price.

regions.title: Sales and collections by product
regions.description: Aggregate order revenue and split it into cash and receivables using the collection rate.

regions.title: Total revenue
regions.description: Current collections feed the cash calculation in Summary.

regions.title: Product unit cost
regions.description: Multiply material usage by unit price and add labor per unit.

regions.title: Cost of goods sold and gross profit
regions.description: Recognize only the cost of units sold in profit.

regions.title: Required production calculation
regions.description: Add sales and safety stock, then deduct opening finished goods to obtain required production.

regions.title: Inventory value and labor
regions.description: Closing inventory remains an asset while production labor is paid from current cash.

regions.title: Material requirement by product
regions.description: Multiply finished production units by material usage per product.

regions.title: Purchase calculation
regions.description: Add safety stock to required units, deduct stock on hand, then apply the purchase price.

regions.title: Total material payments
regions.description: Apply the current payment rate to purchases and send the resulting cash outflow to Summary.

regions.title: Product sales and profit
regions.description: Combine product results from Sales and Costing in one view.

regions.title: Monthly profit
regions.description: Deduct cost of goods sold and fixed operating costs from revenue.

regions.title: Closing cash calculation
regions.description: Combine inflows and outflows to calculate closing cash in P30.

demo.title: Where does closing cash come from?
demo.description: Select the result to reveal sales collections, production and purchasing outflows at their actual worksheet positions.

stops.title: Start here
stops.body: Closing cash is opening cash plus collections, less materials, labor, fixed costs and capital expenditure.

stops.title: Cash coming in
stops.body: Apply the 80% collection rate in Assumptions to each product’s monthly sales.

stops.title: Where revenue starts
stops.body: Apply Catalog prices and each order’s discount to units sold after returns.

stops.title: Orders become production
stops.body: Add units sold and safety stock, then deduct opening finished goods to calculate production.

stops.title: Production becomes materials
stops.body: Multiply production by each product’s material usage. Purchasing combines products that use the same material.

stops.title: Purchases after inventory
stops.body: Add the material safety target and deduct opening stock to calculate new purchases.

stops.title: Purchases become cash outflows
stops.body: Only 65% of purchase units times unit price leaves cash this month.

stops.title: Another cash outflow
stops.body: Sum production units times labor per unit. Cost of goods sold and production labor payments measure different things.

stops.title: The complete calculation
stops.body: Sales collections, material purchases and production labor meet in one result. The flow explains why profit and cash differ.
